content.value_statement: Complex AI work can stall when one agent handles every task. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through agentic-flow swarm patterns for coordinated parallel work.
actual_capabilities: Explains mesh, hierarchical, and adaptive swarm topologies for coordinated agent work.
Shows how to initialize swarms, spawn agents, and orchestrate parallel tasks with agentic-flow.
Defines pipeline patterns with staged dependencies for design, implementation, testing, and review.
Describes shared memory coordination so agents can store and retrieve project state.
Covers load balancing, retry behavior, fallback assignment, performance metrics, and hook integration.
limitations: Requires agentic-flow v1.5.11 or newer and Node.js 18 or newer.
Provides orchestration guidance and examples, not the agentic-flow runtime itself.
Does not validate task safety, package trust, or workspace permissions automatically.
External npx examples should be reviewed and pinned before use in sensitive environments.

use_cases.title: Plan Parallel Feature Delivery
use_cases.description: Split a software feature across coding, testing, review, and architecture agents with clear coordination points.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Complex Automation
use_cases.description: Choose a swarm topology and hook flow for workflows that need shared state and staged execution.

use_cases.title: Improve Multi-Agent Reliability
use_cases.description: Add retry, fallback, load balancing, and monitoring patterns to reduce stalled or uneven agent work.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Small Swarm
prompt_templates.prompt: Use swarm-orchestration to design a three-agent setup for [project]. Include topology, agent roles, and the first task.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Parallel Delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Use swarm-orchestration to split [feature] across coding, testing, and review agents. Include dependencies, timeouts, and coordination points.

prompt_templates.title: Add Shared Memory
prompt_templates.prompt: Use swarm-orchestration to design shared memory keys for [workflow]. Include what each agent writes, reads, and validates.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Resilient Swarm
prompt_templates.prompt: Use swarm-orchestration to compare mesh, hierarchical, and adaptive topologies for [system]. Recommend load balancing, failure handling, and monitoring.

output_examples.input: Plan a swarm for building a REST API with tests.
output: Recommended topology: hierarchical, with an architect coordinating coder, tester, and reviewer agents.
Execution plan: design first, then implementation and tests in parallel, followed by review.
Coordination state: store API schema, test status, review notes, and unresolved risks in shared memory.

output_examples.input: Improve a swarm that has slow agents and uneven task queues.
output_examples.output: Switch to adaptive topology, enable dynamic load balancing, set task timeouts, and track throughput, latency, and agent utilization.

output_examples.input: Recover when one implementation agent fails during a workflow.
output_examples.output: Use exponential retry for transient failures, reassign the task after repeated failure, and record the incident in shared memory.

best_practices: Start with two or three agents before increasing swarm size.
Use shared memory for schemas, decisions, status, and unresolved risks.
Set timeouts, monitor metrics, and define fallback behavior before long runs.
anti_patterns: Starting many agents without clear roles, ownership, or task boundaries.
Using parallel execution when tasks have unresolved dependencies.
Running external hook commands without reviewing package source and workspace impact.

faq.question: Does this skill install agentic-flow?
faq.answer: No. It describes workflows and commands. You need agentic-flow and Node.js available in your environment.

faq.question: Can it run multiple agents automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide orchestration patterns. Actual execution depends on agentic-flow and the tools available in your workspace.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is written for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it only for coding tasks?
faq.answer: No. The examples focus on software delivery, but the topology patterns can support other coordinated workflows.

faq.question: What should I check before running commands?
faq.answer: Review the package source, pin trusted versions when possible, and understand what each hook command will change.

faq.question: Can it handle failed agents?
faq.answer: It includes guidance for retry, fallback, and reassignment strategies. Your runtime must implement those controls.
